cases.notes: In sample apps the receiver is a picklist field in a form on-load workflow, not list.select. Not in the import: Creator rejects the GoldenRow_Select workflow block. Paste Tag.select("Open"); by hand on GoldenRow, on add, on load. It does not return JSON.
Sort pattern: `<fetch>.<Field> sort by <Field>` with no direction. Capture sorts the fetch, then projects Name, so the order is a list.
cases.script:
rows = GoldenRow[Qty != 99] sort by Name;
golden = rows.Name.getAll();

cases.notes: Sort pattern: `<fetch>.<Field> sort by <Field> desc`. Same projection as sort.by-asc.
cases.script:
rows = GoldenRow[Qty != 99] sort by Name desc;
golden = rows.Name.getAll();

cases.notes: Sort pattern: `sort by <Date_field> desc range from 1 to 1`. Projects Qty. The section-3 rows make a Name list ["Ada"] whether or not the sort ran (first inserted row and the Qty 5 row are both Ada). Sorted range is [5]; the unsorted first row is Qty 2.
cases.script:
rows = GoldenRow[Qty != 99] sort by Qty desc range from 1 to 1;
golden = rows.Qty.getAll();

cases.notes: Sort pattern: `for each i in <Form> sort by <Field> { ... }`. A bare collection name is split by this parser. The criteria fetch is the statement it does accept.

Criteria pattern: a bare decision-box name as its own && term. A local is not a field, and Creator rejects the function at save. Billable and Approved are checkbox fields on FlagRow. Sorted by Name because parity.mjs sameValue is isDeepStrictEqual, not a set compare.
cases.script:
rows = FlagRow[Status == "Open" && Billable && Approved] sort by Name;
golden = rows.Name.getAll();

cases.notes: A local set to false is not a criteria term. The usual false term is `<Field> == false` on a decision box. Billable is a checkbox on FlagRow. Only the Dee row is false, so ["Dee"] means the comparison ran. An empty form is also [].
cases.script:
rows = FlagRow[Qty != 99 && Billable == false] sort by Name;
golden = rows.Name.getAll();

cases.notes: Criteria pattern: `ID != input.<Field>` beside other terms. A local replaces input. The field stays on the left. Sorted by Qty so the list is ["Cy","Bea"] (Qty -1 then 0), not the insertion order ["Bea","Cy"]. The harness does not compare getAll lists as a set.

getAll pattern: `<Form>[<decision_box>].<Field>.getAll()`. GoldenRow.Status is text, and a text field with no operator does not save. Billable is a checkbox on FlagRow. A lone name in brackets is an index to this parser, so `sort by` would be a task:sort todo; `Billable == true` is the same decision-box test and accepts the sort. Insertion order of the true rows is Cy, Ada, Bea; the list is Ada, Bea, Cy. The common subform form `input.<subform>.<field>.getall()` is not in this function.
cases.script:
rows = FlagRow[Billable == true] sort by Name;
golden = rows.Name.getAll();
